verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Sivakasi printing units tied to fireworks packaging and education demand, with monthly stock and receivables checks; avoid units with no PESO-linked order book or heavy term debt.
title: Sivakasi printing & publishing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Sivakasi printing runs on two demand engines: fireworks cartons and labels, and school and textbook work.** The town makes the bulk of India's organised fireworks, about 85% of the organised segment [1], and printing, packaging and transport livelihoods ride on it [1]. Paper and ink are the main inputs and both are price-volatile, so margins move with input costs unless contracts carry an escalation clause [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit has a price-escalation clause with its buyers; if it sells only on fixed-price annual contracts, ask how it absorbed the last paper spike.**

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Cash is trapped in festival-season receivables and paper stock, not in the press.** Fireworks demand peaks around Diwali [2][3], so printers build stock and extend credit to cracker units months before cash comes back. Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap [D], and India-wide printing output (NIC 17) is -0.1% YoY [D]. **So favour units with a named export or green-cracker buyer and a PESO-compliant unit; avoid pure domestic cracker-label printers with one large buyer.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure short: cash credit against stock and receivables, no long tenor for seasonal working capital.** Rating commentary on print peers flags working capital intensity of 41.1% of operating income in FY2025 [8] and continuous technology spend as a cash drain [10].
